gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Jackery HomePower 3000, the only pick at 3 kWh whose TT-30 carries a full 30 A, costs $1,499 at jackery.com today. That is $200 less than the Anker SOLIX F3000 ($1,699.99 on Amazon), the other full-30 A 3 kWh unit, and $1,300 less than the $2,799 ChatGPT showed for the DELTA Pro 3. The $949.99 Anker C2000 Gen 2's TT-30R stops at 20 A (2,400 W).
standout_why: SolutionEnergy (cited) prices only the DELTA Pro 3 (about $2,799, Oct 2026) and the DELTA 3 Plus (about $669). It says 'check current price' for the C2000 Gen 2, AC200L and HomePower 3000. QuietTechReport (cited) gives no prices at all. Both pages say the HomePower 3000's TT-30 is full 30 A and the C2000 Gen 2's is 20 A, so the outlet ratings are not new. What is new is today's price on every candidate, the cost per Wh, and the fact that the cheapest full-30 A 3 kWh unit costs about half as much as ChatGPT's 'heavy-duty' pick.
decides: This confirms the HomePower 3000 as the pick for a trailer owner who wants the whole 30 A plug at 3 kWh. It is cheaper than the F3000 and the DELTA Pro 3, and QuietTechReport lists it at 59.5 lb against 91.5 lb and 113.5 lb. It loses only on expansion: SolutionEnergy and QuietTechReport both say it can't take extra batteries. Shoppers who only run the fridge, lights and outlets can drop to a 2 kWh unit for $879 to $950, accepting the 20 A outlet limit or no RV outlet at all. The BLUETTI AC200L, ChatGPT's 'best value' card, shows as unavailable at $899 in BLUETTI's own store today.
